cards.explanation: The answer is that they ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD for them. Zedekiah, king of Judah, sends Pashhur and the priest Zephaniah to Jeremiah, the prophet. Their words are, “Please inquire of the LORD on our behalf, since Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is waging war against us.” Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon, and his army is the reason for the visit. I think a city with an army at its door gets very interested in what a prophet has to say.

The answer is True. Zedekiah's men say, “Perhaps the LORD will perform for us something like all His past wonders, so that Nebuchadnezzar will withdraw from us.” That word “Perhaps” tells you they're hoping. They want the LORD to act the way He has before. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is the one they want to see pack up and leave.

The answer is the weapons in their own hands. The LORD says, “I will turn against you the weapons of war in your hands…” Those weapons are what Zedekiah's people are using against the Chaldeans, Babylon's people, who besiege the city from outside the wall. The very weapons they are holding are the ones the LORD says He will turn against them. He names the weapons, and He doesn't name anything else here.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “And I Myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a mighty arm, with anger, fury, and great wrath.” He isn't fighting for Zedekiah's side. He is fighting against them. Zedekiah's men were hoping for a wonder like the ones in the past, and this isn't the kind they hoped for. This is a heavy part, friends.

The answer is that he will not spare them. The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar “…will put them to the sword; he will not spare them or show pity or compassion.” The ones handed over are Zedekiah, his officers and the people who survive the plague and sword and famine. This is a heavy verse, friends. I think this one hurts.

The answer is whoever goes out and surrenders. The LORD says, “…whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who besiege you will live; he will retain his life like a spoil of war.” That's a strange path, because going out looks like giving up. But it's the way of life the LORD set before them in verse 8. Staying in the city is the other way.

The answer is fire. The LORD says the city “…will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, who will destroy it with fire.” Fire turns up again in this passage when the LORD speaks to the house of David. I know fire from my ovens, friends, and this isn't the cozy kind. This is a serious word.

The answer is justice. The LORD says, “Administer justice every morning, and rescue the victim of robbery from the hand of his oppressor…” He speaks it to the house of David, the royal family. It's a daily job, not a once in a while one. I think a person who's rescued from an oppressor would be glad it was every morning.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…or My wrath will go forth like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it because of their evil deeds.” That's the other side of the daily job of justice. The house of David is the one being warned.

The answer is that they say no one can come against them. They say, “Who can come against us? Who can enter our dwellings?” I think that's the talk of people who feel safe up on their rocky plateau. I bet a great view can make a person feel pretty tall. But the LORD says, “Behold, I am against you…”

The answer is foreigners, the fatherless and widows. The LORD says, “Do no wrong or violence to the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow.” He says it right after telling the king to rescue the victim of robbery. These are people who might not have much to stand on, and the LORD names them one by one. I think that tells us they matter to Him.

The answer is True. The LORD says that if they carry out these commands, “…kings who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this palace riding on chariots and horses…” It's a good picture, with kings coming in with their officials and their people. This is the bright side of the big IF. It all hangs on carrying out the commands.

The answer is a pile of rubble. The LORD says, “…I swear by Myself, declares the LORD, that this house will become a pile of rubble.” He swears by Himself, which is as serious as it gets. This is the other side of the IF. The word is for the king, his officials and his people.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “…I will surely turn you into a desert, like cities that are uninhabited.” He says “surely,” so there's no maybe in it. Right before this He calls the house like Gilead and like the summit of Lebanon. It's a big drop from there to a desert, friends.

The answer is cedars. The LORD says the destroyers “…will cut down the choicest of your cedars and throw them into the fire.” These destroyers come, each man with his weapons. Cedars are tall trees, and the choicest ones are named. A timber pile has never looked so sad.

The answer is that they forsook the LORD's covenant and served other gods. People will reply, “Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God and have worshiped and served other gods.” Many nations pass by and ask why, and this is the answer given. It's the reason in the text, plain and simple. A covenant is a promise the LORD made with His people, and they turned from it.
